title: RAW UNREVIEWED: tricoccum seed preserves one loin effect across topical and decoction routes
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Pliny XXII.29 assigns the tricoccum seed a topical action drawing corrupt blood from the vertebrae and loins, then explicitly says a decoction taken in chicken broth or with beet and lentils produces a similar effect. Seed husks separately restore natural skin colour to lividities. Preserve the cross-route effect equivalence and husk-specific endpoint, rather than flattening the passage into a generic internal/external list.

source.observed_content: The tricoccum seed, applied topically, draws corrupt blood from vertebrae and loins; a decoction of that seed taken in chicken broth or with beet/lentils has a similar effect. The seed husks restore natural colour to lividities.
source.layer: Retained modern English translation of an ancient primary; not a fresh Latin or medieval witness collation

potential_admitted_target: None asserted; root must separately nominate any permitted complete unit before review.

design.mechanism: Keep the tricoccum seed as the material subject across a topical operation and an oral decoction branch; bind both routes to the same stated vertebra/loin effect. Keep the husks (not the seed preparation generally) attached to a distinct skin-colour outcome. The source's explicit 'similar effect' is the nontrivial constraint: route and carrier change while the effect remains stable, but the subpart branch changes the result.
design.unit: Complete Pliny XXII.29 chapter paragraph 3, preserving the explicit tricoccum subject and its local preceding boundary from helioscopium.
design.observable_consequence: A future whole-unit reading could use this model only if one material participant remains bound to two differently routed preparations with the same specific result and a separately owned husk result. A reading that assigns one outcome per adjacent operation, or transfers the colour result to the seed/decoction, fails this source-specific prediction. No target feature is claimed to exist.
design.scope: Source-only raw hypothesis; unreviewed, unselected and untested; no target glosses

execution_requirements: Root first selects a permitted complete unit and owns any target inspection; this producer did not access one.
Test the same-effect relation across route/carrier alternatives separately from part-to-colour assignment.
Retain rival readings with separate effects for each route and a generic plant-preparation account; do not repair absent links with free glosses.
Treat all medical statements as historical claims, not clinical facts.
assumptions_and_limits: The source translation's 'other kind' in paragraph 3 is tricoccum/scorpiuron; botanical modern identification remains disputed in the included edition notes.
The phrase 'similar effect' links the decoction to the seed's preceding vertebra/loin claim; no stronger mechanism is stated.
The source is in the Bostock/Riley 1856 English translation, not a fresh Latin or medieval manuscript collation.

IDEA000784 treats other plant-carriage/knot operations in the same Pliny chapter; IDEA000801 treats a different helioscopium bowel-preparation gradient. This proposal is a distinct cross-route same-result constraint but remains subject to review for source-family overlap.
